meaning:
χιτών, ῶνος, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for כְּתֹנֶת:]
the garment worn next the skin (though two tunics were sometimes worn, see Swete, Mk., 117), a tunic: Mat.10:10, Mrk.6:9 14:63, Luk.3:11 9:3, Ju 23; dieting. from ἱμάτιον (which see), Mat.5:40, Luk.6:29, Jhn.19:23, Act.9:39 (see DCG, i, 338, 340, 499)
(AS)

elsewhere.note: If anyone sues you to take away your coat, let him have your cloak also.
but to wear sandals, and not put on two tunics.
He answered them, “He who has two coats, let him give to him who has none. He who has food, let him do likewise.”
Then the soldiers, when they had crucified Jesus, took his garments and made four parts, to every soldier a part; and also the coat. Now the coat was without…
Peter got up and went with them. When he had come, they brought him into the upper room. All the widows stood by him weeping, and showing the coats and…
and some save, snatching them out of the fire with fear, hating even the clothing stained by the flesh.
